Recompence
REK-om-pens
noun
The Authorized Version’s spelling of recompense, from the Latin recompensare — re, back, and compensare, to weigh together. A recompence is a weighing-back: requital rendered in exact proportion, whether of reward or of punishment.

Biblical Definition

Recompence is requital weighed out, and Scripture assigns it emphatically to God. “To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence; their foot shall slide in due time” (Deu 32:35) — a verse Paul quotes to forbid private revenge: “avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord” (Rom 12:19). The logic is not that vengeance is wrong in itself but that it belongs to Someone, and taking it is theft as much as sin. The same word then does duty in the gospel. To the fearful Isaiah says, “Be strong, fear not: behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence; he will come and save you” (Isa 35:4). Notice how that verse is built: the recompence and the salvation are the same coming. God’s settling of accounts is the deliverance of the oppressed, which is why the poor and the persecuted in Scripture pray for judgment rather than dreading it. Solomon states the principle in ordinary life — “the recompence of a man’s hands shall be rendered unto him” (Pro 12:14) — and Job warns that for the deceived, “vanity shall be his recompence” (Job 15:31), a man paid back in the very currency he chose.

Webster 1828 Definition

Requital weighed back in proportion — reward or punishment. In Scripture, chiefly God’s prerogative, and the reason private revenge is forbidden.

RECOMPENCE, RECOMPENSE, n. An equivalent returned for anything given, done, or suffered.

Compensation; reward; amends for injury or loss.

Requital; retribution; punishment weighed to the offence.

From the Latin re and compensare, to weigh together, to counterbalance.

Deu 32:35: To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence.

Key Scripture

Deu 32:35 — "To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence; their foot shall slide in due time: for the day of their calamity is at hand, and the things that shall come upon them make haste."

Pro 12:14 — "A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth: and the recompence of a man's hands shall be rendered unto him."

Isa 35:4 — "Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence; he will come and save you."

Rom 12:19 — "Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord."

Modern Corruption

Divine retribution is dismissed as unworthy of a loving God, which removes the only ground Scripture gives the wronged for laying down their own vengeance.

expand to see more

The corruption is the sentimental rejection of retribution. It is widely held that a God of love cannot also be a God who repays, and that the language of vengeance belongs to a primitive stratum of religion the church should outgrow. The dictionary rejects this. It is not merely that Scripture teaches divine recompence from Deuteronomy to Revelation; it is that removing it makes the New Testament’s ethics impossible. Paul’s command not to avenge oneself rests entirely on the promise that God will: avenge not yourselves, for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay. Take away the second clause and the first is not mercy but a demand that the wronged accept permanent injustice.

Recover the plain sense: the doctrine of recompence is what makes forgiveness possible for people who have suffered real wrongs. A man can release his grip on a debt precisely because he knows the books will be balanced by One who sees what he cannot and judges without error. He is not asked to pretend the wrong did not happen or that it does not matter; he is asked to hand it to the proper court. And Isa 35:4 shows the same truth in its gospel dress: the coming that brings recompence is the coming that saves, so that for those who trust Him the settling of accounts is not a terror but a rescue. The oppressed in Scripture do not fear the judgment. They pray, How long, O Lord?

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Latin re + compensare, to weigh back — exact requital; God’s prerogative, and the ground on which revenge is forbidden.

expand to see more

Recompence — the AV spelling; Latin recompensare, to weigh back.

The image is a balance: requital weighed to the offence or the service.

Deu 32:35, quoted at Rom 12:19 to forbid private revenge.

Pro 12:14: the recompence of a man’s hands shall be rendered unto him.

Isa 35:4 joins recompence and salvation in one coming.

Usage

"Revenge is forbidden because it belongs to God, not because requital is wrong."

"Isa 35:4: the coming with recompence is the coming that saves."

"The doctrine is what makes forgiveness possible for the genuinely wronged."
